subject: decision on constraint/dimension variable declaration syntax

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: decision on constraint/dimension variable declaration syntax
parts:
I've thought about it and talked to Daniel and concluded
that we should go with the following syntax, which uses
square brackets for all dimensions and angle brackets for
constraints:

real x[4,5];
real<lower=-1> x[4,5];
real<upper=1> x[4,5];
real<lower=-1,upper=1> x[4,5];

matrix[2,3] m[4,5];
matrix<lower=-1>[2,3] m[4,5];
matrix<upper=1>[2,3] m[4,5];
matrix<lower=-1,upper=1>[2,3] m[4,5];

matrix<scalar=int,lower=0>[2,3] m[4,5];

The default bounds are -infinity() and infinity()
for real and -Integer.MAX and +Integer.MAX for
integers. (I just now realized I should put
constants for those in Stan.)

I find the above proposal is easier to scan
visually than if we use square brackets for constraints:

real[lower=-1,upper=1] x[4,5];
matrix[lower=-1,upper=1][2,3] x[4,5];

Given that we're already known as the language that
uses semicolons, I'll try to shrug off the brackets
by avoiding this:

real[bounds=[-1,]] x[4,5];
real[bounds=[,1]] x[4,5];
real[bounds=[-1,1]] x[4,5];

or even this

real<bounds=[-1,]> x[4,5];
real<bounds=[,1]> x[4,5];
real<bounds=[-1,1]> x[4,5];

It's a bit more work than adding bounds=, but I think
it'll be worth it. I'll make sure you can do it in
the opposite order, too:

real<upper=1,lower=-1> x[4,5];

- Bob
